'''Toktayum Umetalieva''' ({{langx|ky|Токтайым Уметалиева}}) (born 4 April 1962 in [[Bakay-Ata|Leninpol]]) is a Kyrgyzstani physicist, political coordinator and activist. She was the only female candidate for the [[2005 Kyrgyz presidential election|2005]] and [[2009 Kyrgyz presidential election]]s.<ref name="knews">{{cite web|date=August 2011|title=Токтайым Уметалиева|url=http://knews.kg/2011/08/umetalieva-toktayyim-djumakovna/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210808174945/https://knews.kg/2011/08/15/umetalieva-toktayyim-djumakovna/|archive-date=2021-08-08|website=Knews|publisher=Knews|language=Kyrgyz|accessdate=27 November 2017}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in the village of Leninpol in [[Talas District, Kyrgyzstan|Talas District]], she graduated from [[Kyrgyz State National University]] with a degree in physics in 1984. She worked a lecturer and became a director for an industrial and commercial company. In 1997, she was appointed chief editor of the newspaper ''Ай-Данек'',<ref name="ca"/> and she has published several papers on science and politics.<ref name="knews"/> She has sat on numerous advisory councils in her native country for [[Supreme Council (Kyrgyzstan)|Supreme Council]] and has led the political party known as "Long Live Kyrgyzstan" ("Жашасын Кыргызстан").<ref name="ca">{{cite web|date=2017-01-24|title=Toktayum Umetalieva|url=https://centralasien.org/en/40-women-of-kyrgyzstan-portraits/toktayum-umetalieva/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210808175036/https://centralasien.org/en/40-women-of-kyrgyzstan-portraits/toktayum-umetalieva/|archive-date=2021-08-08|website=Centralasien Grupperna|publisher=Centralasien.org|accessdate=27 November 2017}}</ref>

She heads the [[Association of Nongovernmental and Noncommercial Organizations]] and was running as an independent.<ref>
{{cite web|date=July 8, 2005|title=Q&A: Kyrgyzstan votes|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/4664827.stm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309120800/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/4664827.stm|archive-date=2018-03-09|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=2009-07-28}}</ref>

Umetalieva been employed as a national coordinator for [[UNICEF]] and is associated with the [[World Bank]]. Between 2000 and 2010 she was the chair of Kyrgyzstan's Association of Nongovernmental and Noncommercial Organizations. She stood as a presidential candidate for the 2009 elections to raise awareness of [[women's rights]] issues.<ref name="ca"/> In 2011 she advocated the dismantling of the statue of Erkindik on [[Ala-Too Square]] in [[Bishkek]].<ref name="knews"/>

She is married and has three daughters: Mirgul, Nazgul, and Burulayim.<ref name="knews"/>
